pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Score.tsx:157 A cue the music vendor refused and a cue nobody has rendered both draw as "missing" (and the cut's ClipView status is only ok|missing|drift), so a refused region is never a drawn state of the cut with its cost, which is exactly the collapse gap-and-refusal-honesty forbids.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Score.tsx:157 Missing is drawn in place, which is good, but there is no refused state: refused-by-provider and never-requested are merged into one look.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Cut.tsx:114 The only nudge step is ±50 ms on a 25 fps cut (a 40 ms frame), so it is not the sub-frame step the technique requires. Snap-to-mark (line 118) and the signed offset readout are present.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Cut.tsx:169 Picture, voice and music lanes keep a fixed order (LANES at line 30) on one CutClock. Blocks are drawn to scale from drawnS, the same value the offset readout edits.
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Score.tsx:47 Each cue carries a stated purpose and a tempo, and its span is first-to-last scene (snapped to scene marks), so it moves with the picture.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Score.tsx:253 The derived turn is drawn once on the shared ruler. An absent turn draws no mark rather than zero. The derivation itself lives in the fixtures/lib (see part-port-fixtures).
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Render.tsx:76 An undecodable still no longer leaves a blank canvas under a 'poster preview' label. It becomes an error that names the input.
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Render.tsx:62 The poster preview runs the export's own compositor frame function in the browser before the priced mv render job.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Motion.tsx:99 Motion for a still is a proposal with moves, held-still elements and model/vendor provenance. A decline to animate is shown verbatim (line 85), and a re-drawn plate marks the outcome stale.

pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureScore.ts:65 The score's turn takes the first scene whose mood matches /turn/ without surfacing a second match. It is also a second derivation beside the cut's turnOf (fixtureCut.ts:143), so the same structural fact has two derivations that can age apart.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureScore.ts:65 The turn is derived from material, and absence gives null, but two matches silently take the first, and this derivation is separate from turnOf, breaking 'one derivation, all consumers'.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureCut.ts:123 Offsets are stored as data and snap returns to exactly 0. But status only flips drift->ok at zero, and deriveTimeline never emits drift for a project, so a clip nudged 300 ms off its mark still reads ok. The status is not derived from the offset.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureScore.ts:84 Gaps and covered seconds are computed (lines 88-89), but a cue's only failure signal is a null active take. Nothing in the score record or view holds a refused render.
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureCut.ts:121 The drawn start is computed from the same offsets value the bench reports (offsetMs, line 127): same fact, same pixels.
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureScore.ts:265 A cue's take has one section per scene it spans, timed from the picture.
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureCut.ts:100 The cut is compiled to a deterministic EDL whose digest is carried with each export.
